subject: SentryOps renewal: uptake snapshot, performance ROI & signoff checklist
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire.park@sentryops.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@sentryops.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Q1 usage snapshot and renewal window

Hi Karthik —

Attaching our Q1 usage snapshot (see attachment). We had an unexpected 45% spike in inference calls after the June release; a lot of that is short-chat traffic but also an increase in longer-context calls for our summarization flow.

Can you help translate this into committed capacity options? We're looking at a renewal in early June and want to avoid surprise overages. High-level asks:
- A rough per-million-token cost at current model mix (text+chat+embeddings)
- Any short-term burst / bridge options if we decide to commit at a lower level
- Whether dedicated pools would materially change latency for our 2k token average prompts

Attachment: sentry-q1-usage-report.pdf (pdf, 42KB)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.
Claire
Director, Platform Engineering
SentryOps
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@sentryops.ai>
Cc: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-18T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q1 usage snapshot and renewal window

Claire — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Quick read-through: the spike looks driven by ramped-up nightly batch jobs + interactive summarization. I attached a short slide deck with a one-page ROI recap and three commit paths (conservative, target, aggressive).

Highlights up front:
- Ballpark per-million-token cost (current model mix): $95–$115 depending on burst usage and cache hit rate.
- If you lock a 6-month commit at the target path we model ~22% unit-cost savings vs current on-demand.
- Dedicated pools will reduce 95p latency by ~30–40ms for your 2k median requests in our benchmarks; worth considering if tail latency matters for your SLAs.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call tomorrow to pick a path and confirm model mix (20m)
2) I’ll draft a proposed term sheet and DocuSign for review
3) Engineering check with Naomi on the latency benchmarks and warm/cache behavior

Attachment: sentry-kpi-slide-deck.pptx (pptx, 1.2MB)

If that works, what time tomorrow (PST) is best?

—Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SentryOps commit sizing questions

Karthik / Tessa — quick internal note after reviewing Claire's report and your deck. A couple of clarifications we need before we send a firm term: 

1) Model mix: Are they running a small portion of high-context summarization on the longer LLM (30% of tokens) or is that an edge case? If it's heavier, the unit-cost curve changes materially.
2) Cache characteristic: Their nightly batch looks like it could reap big wins from prefix caching; need request fingerprint sample. That could pull the per-million down ~12–18%.
3) SLA/latency: Naomi, can you confirm our bench on dedicated pools at 2k tokens median (I pulled 95p from the deck but want the raw numbers and expected warm-cache behavior).

I attached a redline of the proposed term we usually push for mid-market renewals (short form + burst credits). If SentryOps wants the bridge option, we should price a 3-month bridge with reduced discount and a clear uplift trigger.

Attachment: proposed-commit-term-redline.docx (docx, 85KB)

We should keep this lightweight and give them 48 hours to decide once we hand off the DocuSign.

—Jasmine
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@sentryops.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: SentryOps Legal <legal@sentryops.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-20T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: SentryOps renewal — proposed commit, bridge option, and signoff checklist

Claire — thank you and team for the extra context. Per our internal review (see thread below), here is a proposal that balances runway protection and flexibility: 

Proposal (6 month term, start June 1):
- Committed tokens: 120M tokens / month
- Unit price (blended, estimated): $92 per million tokens (post-cache adjustments)*
- Burst buffer: 20M tokens/month at on-demand rate (no discount) — used automatically, billed monthly
- Dedicated pool pilot: optional 2-week pilot during month 1 (we'll provision a dedicated lane if you opt in)

Bridge option (if you want to delay a full commit):
- 3-month bridge at 65% of the full commit level, with a step-up clause to convert to the 6-month term mid-bridge if usage surpasses 85% for two consecutive weeks.

Next actions: 
1) Confirm model mix by EOD Monday — we need to know % long-context summarization vs short chat to finalize blended pricing.
2) If you accept the 6-month path above, we will send a DocuSign (link below) with a one-week review window.
3) Naomi will share dedicated pool latency bench and caching assumptions in a short appendix to the DocuSign.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/REDACTED/sentry-commit-2028
Drive slides + dashboard: https://drive.google.com/s/REDACTED/sentry-q1-dashboard
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/SENT-2028-04
